item.text:
**Verdict:** Yes. In 2024 Xi’s system used surveillance, digital controls, and administrative harassment to narrow political space. I found no credible evidence of a nationwide internet shutdown; the control pattern was more selective and continuous: censorship, platform throttling, real-name/AI labeling rules, policing of activists, and pressure on independent media and civil society.

| Valence | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Weak positive / official claim | **Beijing says counterterrorism measures are grounded in law and protect human rights** | State Council Information Office / China Xinjiang | 2024-01-23 | https://en.chinaxinjiang.cn/2024/01/23/c03755707ff440c3be77630f280ae0a0.html | Officially claims counterterrorism is lawful and human-rights-protecting. This is self-justification, not independent evidence that surveillance was restrained. | 4B.9 |
| Strong negative | **关于开展“清朗·整治‘自媒体’无底线博流量”专项行动的通知** | Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission Office / CAC | 2024-04-23 | https://www.cac.gov.cn/2024-04/23/c_1715545670217049.htm | Orders real-name verification, source labeling, AI labeling, traffic throttling, suspension of comments/likes, and account closures for “self-media.” This is direct digital control over political speech. | 4B.9, 4B.6 |
| Strong negative | **RFA shuts Hong Kong bureau after security-law concerns** | Reuters | 2024-03-29 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/usfunded-radio-free-asia-shuts-hong-kong-bureau-citing-security-law-concerns-3358157 | Reports RFA closed its Hong Kong bureau after Article 23 raised staff-safety concerns; Hong Kong officials had called RFA a “foreign force.” This is administrative and legal pressure that chilled independent reporting. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.3 |
| Strong negative | **Hong Kong 47 democrats case** | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427 | Reports extensive pretrial detention, denial of bail, and mass convictions of opposition figures. This is political harassment through legal process, not neutral law enforcement. | 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.7, 4B.4 |
| Strong negative | **China: Religious regulations tighten Uyghurs** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-31 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/31/china-religious-regulations-tighten-uyghurs | Says revised religious rules intensify “Sinicization,” threaten imprisonment for noncompliance, and sit inside a broader surveillance regime. This is coercive minority control using administrative and surveillance tools. | 4B.9, 4B.7, 4B.4 |
| Strong negative | **China: Overseas students face harassment and surveillance** | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/china-overseas-students-face-harassment-and-surveillance-in-campaign-of-transnational-repression/ | Describes Chinese authorities photographing, following, and pressuring students abroad and targeting families in China to deter activism. This is direct surveillance used for intimidation. | 4B.9, 4B.7, 4B.6 |
| Strong negative | **Hong Kong human rights situation deteriorated** | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128576.html | The report says 2024 saw arbitrary arrest and detention, censorship, transnational repression, and coercive actions against independent trade unions and labor activists. This is the broadest summary evidence of political-freedom suppression. | 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.7, 4B.4, 4B.6 |
| Strong negative | **China: Freedom in the World 2024** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-world/2024 | Says China has one of the world’s most restrictive media environments and a sophisticated censorship system, including direct party control, directives, website blocks, app removal, and mass deletions. This is the clearest general evidence of digital censorship. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.3 |

**Search gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence of a nationwide internet shutdown in China.
- The stronger record is selective but pervasive: platform controls, censorship, surveillance, and harassment rather than a single countrywide outage.
